note: H3 song lock: a performer lip-syncs to a song you bring, and the song stays bit-exact. Measured proof: studio/song_lock_proof.json (GET /api/song-lock).

recipes.title: Song Lock: bring your song
recipes.pitch: Your finished song and one performer: MiniMax H3 makes them sing it in three shots, and your song comes out of the edit bit-exact. Lip-sync is still weak.
recipes.why: The song is never regenerated. Each shot hands H3 its stretch of the song as a locked audio latent (noise mask 0) plus an audio keyframe, so H3 only draws a picture that sings what is already there. Then the studio cuts that stretch from your original file sample by sample, joins the pictures without re-encoding them and muxes the stretch as FLAC. The cut step hashes the decoded samples of the result against the original stretch and refuses to finish if they differ.

tips: Bring your own song on the first step and your performer on the second. Only songs you own or control, and only a performer who is invented or who has agreed in writing.
A lossless song (WAV or FLAC) comes out bit-exact. An MP3 or M4A is decoded once, so the result matches the decoded song, which is all a lossy file can promise.
Pick a stretch with singing in it. With 'auto' the studio takes the loudest stretch, which is usually a chorus.
Slow camera moves keep the face, and so the mouth, in frame.

steps.label: Your song
steps.prompt:
Global Metadata
Basic Attributes: bpm is 92. key is A, and scale is major. Warm indie folk pop.
Global Emotional Progression: A close, quiet verse grows into a bright, open chorus and settles again at the end.
Sonics & Production Profile: Warm and intimate, the lead vocal close and clear in the middle of the mix.
Vocal Details
Vocal Gender & Timbre: Singer A (Female), warm and clear.
Vocal Style: Plain, unhurried, every word sung clearly and in order.
Arrangement
Primary: Fingerpicked acoustic guitar and a soft kick.
Secondary: Upright bass and a light string pad in the chorus.

steps.label: Your performer
steps.prompt: Waist-up portrait photo of {performer}, facing the camera with a calm, open expression, mouth closed, soft window light, plain warm background. An invented person. No text, no logos.

steps.label: The stretch to sing
steps.model: ffmpeg and Whisper, on the CPU

proof.note: Status: audio exact, lip-sync weak, working to fix. Measured on 2026-11-03 on an AI song (Music 3) with an invented performer, by programs only (nobody has watched or listened): the song in the finished edit is bit-exact (the sha256 of its decoded samples equals the original stretch's). Lip-sync is weak: each shot's mouth follows its own stretch of the song with a mean best correlation of 0.25, against 0.18 for another stretch of the same song; the earlier studio called 0.35 good. Swapping the turbo LoRA did not change that.
